Orbital Robotics plans ISS capture and servicing demonstrations

The Arkisys collaboration targets a Q3 2027 launch of scaled robotic arms for Astrobee experiments in microgravity.

GeekWire ↗5 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2

Three demonstrations are planned

Seattle startup Orbital Robotics announced on October 5 that it plans to send robotic arms to the International Space Station in Q3 2027. Three demonstrations would take place roughly a month apart. Partner Arkisys would support integration and the Astrobee platform. These are future experiments, not completed satellite repairs.

One Astrobee would service another

Astronauts would install scaled versions of the company’s ORA-A arms on one free-flying Astrobee. It would capture a second Astrobee and replace a simple compute module launched for the experiment. The aim is to evaluate capture hardware and autonomous control software together in microgravity, extending laboratory testing into real spaceflight conditions.

A useful proxy with clear limits

The company says it is funding launch and demonstrations internally, with Arkisys implementing them through its NASA agreement. The arms could remain aboard for cargo handling and further research. Success would support confidence in robotic servicing, but an experiment inside the station is not equivalent to an operational mission repairing a satellite outside it.
